content.text:
I reviewed the transcript against the record and paired each answer-key item.

**Summary of findings**
- All 12 key items are captured by some record item; nothing is missed.
- Corrected figures were handled well: $48,210 (not $84,000), $7,500 (not $7,000), retirement age 58 (not 60), $1,000/month per child.
- Two due dates are wrong: the e-sign packet is recorded as 2026-10-22 when Theo committed to "early next week" (week of Oct 19), and the Margit note is recorded as 2026-10-17, a Saturday, when Renata said "this week" (by Fri Oct 16).
- None of the five declined/parked items (457(b), cash balance plan, superfunding, lake house, 100%-stock allocation) leaked in as actions — clean.
- Extras: the record splits the backdoor Roth into two items and the 529 plan into four, which are legitimate content but split key items; the Rowan soccer tournament is transcript-established chit-chat rather than a planning life event.

key_items.note: Captures partnership effective July 1, 2026, W-2 to K-1 shift and move into partners' 401(k). Omits buy-in from draws over two years and quarterly estimates, but no figure is wrong.
September 2026 announcement and Q1 2027 close are both right; calls it a merger as the clients did. Omits contract honored through June 2028 and benefit harmonization, but nothing stated is wrong.

Uses the corrected balance $48,210, not the initial $84,000 Declan misspoke. Destination (Coldharbor partners' 401(k)) is right; the Dec 31, 2026 deadline is not carried, but no due date is required for an account action.

Priya's leg of the backdoor Roth: $7,500 nondeductible traditional IRA converted to her existing Roth, as soon as the account is open. $7,500 is the corrected 2026 figure, not $7,000. Declan's leg appears separately as record 6 (split).

Opening Callum's 529 is the headline of this key item; amount NOT_FOUND is acceptable since the opening itself carries no figure. The $1,000/month for all three children is split out into records 8, 9 and 10.

Both carriers named correctly (Pellwood spelled as Theo corrected, plus Ashgrove Life); owner Theo Brandvold; due 2026-10-31 matches 'end of the month'. Does not spell out true own-occupation/specialty-specific, but no figure is wrong.
Owner Priya Halloran; due 2026-10-21, the final Wednesday date after she moved it off Friday. Covers both the LTD certificate and the benefits summary.
Correctly reassigned to Theo Brandvold after Renata took Declan off the hook at 00:14:50; due 2026-10-15 matches Theo's 'answer for you by Thursday'. Includes obtaining the roll-in form.

Owner Theo is right and scope (new IRAs, rollover paperwork, 529s) matches. Due date is wrong: Theo committed to having the packet out 'early next week' (week of Oct 19), but the record says 2026-10-22, a Thursday, which is effectively end of that week and conflates with Declan's Oct 23 deadline.

Uses the corrected retirement age 58, not the stale 60; owner Renata Oakhurst; due 2026-11-26 matches 'before Thanksgiving'. Does not mention the simultaneous college-funding rerun with the new 529 amounts, but the core task and all figures are right.

Owner Renata is right and the 8606/1099-R content matches. Due date is wrong: Renata said she would send Margit a note 'this week' (meeting was Tuesday Oct 13, so by Friday Oct 16); the record says 2026-10-17, which is the Saturday after.

Owner Declan Halloran, source Marisa Quennell, both documents (partner group LTD certificate and the disability section of the partnership agreement) captured; due 2026-10-23 matches 'end of next week'.

extra_items.note: The transcript establishes it: Rowan, age ten, had a tournament in Fredericksburg on Saturday, three games, lost the last on penalties as fourth kicker (soccer is a fair inference). Factually supported, though it is rapport chit-chat rather than a planning-relevant life event.

Declan's leg of the same single backdoor Roth key item already paired at record 4; the record splits one agreed action ($7,500 each, $15,000 total) into two. Content itself is accurate, including the December timing after the rollover zeroes his IRA.
Split of the single 529 key item paired at record 7. Content is accurate (Rowan increased from $500 to $1,000 a month).
Split of the single 529 key item paired at record 7. Content is accurate (Ivy increased from $500 to $1,000 a month).
Split of the single 529 key item paired at record 7; also overlaps record 7's own Callum account. Content is accurate ($1,000 a month for Callum, first draft Nov 1).
